v2:752aa28e01494edde9bdeae00c6bb4c06c924.method: Streamed 1174 jsonl files (14 main, 1160 subagent) across the 6 stores, 126,132 lines in total. Prefiltered lines containing tool_use or tool_result, skipped api-request-blob and file-history lines, and skipped assistant lines whose model is synthetic. tool_use blocks are deduped by id and tool_result blocks by tool_use_id, matched within each file. Result size is the string length, or the sum of text-block lengths, of the result content. The 'sub' side is every file under /subagents/. 15 tool_use calls have no result (counted with 0 chars). Shell category checks run in this order: git (diff/show/log/status/blame is git-read, any other git is shell-write); search words; run words (python3 is included); file-read words, which become shell-write if the command has a heredoc or a file redirect; then cp/mv/rm/mkdir or any heredoc/redirect/Set-Content as shell-write; the rest is shell-other. Leading cd (with &&, ; or newline) and env-var prefixes are stripped before taking the first word.
v2:752aa28e01494edde9bdeae00c6bb4c06c924.caveats: Result chars are characters, not tokens. ToolSearch results are reference blocks with no text, so they count as 0 chars. The first-word breakdown still has about 482 'cd' entries (a cd with no recognized separator) and 176 empty first words, which land in shell-other. shell-other (1,855 calls) also holds first words like for, echo, awk, mkdir-less commands, and project scripts. One call used a 'Powershell' tool name with different casing (1 call, kept separate and categorized as other, 9 other calls total). Files contain about 1 GB, not 2 GB, for FixFlow.

v2:cb617df2c43aa5b63d5bb0dad1eca37c53449.repo: Clinic Workshop (24_Clinic_Workshop testbed): 20 transcript stores (the main store, 18 worktree stores found by the glob, and the OneDrive store)
v2:cb617df2c43aa5b63d5bb0dad1eca37c53449.method: I wrote a streaming Node script (readline, 8 files read at once). It walks every .jsonl file under the 20 store folders. A file sitting at the top of a store folder counts as main. A file under /subagents/workflows/ counts as workflow, and any other file under /subagents/ counts as an Agent-tool subagent. No file fell outside these three groups. The script skips api-request-blob and file-history lines. It counts compact_boundary system lines, and keeps the last cost-state line in each main file. An API call is an assistant line with message.usage whose model is not <synthetic>. Calls are deduplicated by message.id across all files at once. For a repeated id, each usage field takes the highest value seen. Context is input + cache_write + cache_read. The month comes from the timestamp on the first line seen for each id. Per-model thinking tokens: opus-5-5 10,663,219; sonnet-5-5 2,865,971; fable-5-1 719,348; fable-5-2 44,825; haiku-5-5 11,606; opus-4-8 9,147. Per-role thinking tokens: main 4,781,879; agent 4,690,811; workflow 4,841,426. Per-month thinking tokens: 2026-10 6,033,276; 2026-11 8,280,840. Results were written to result.json in the same folder. Cost-state check: 34 of the 41 main files have a cost-state line, and their last totalCostUSD values add up to $1,302.54. The second script in that folder, dupcheck.js, checks how the repeated lines differ.
v2:cb617df2c43aa5b63d5bb0dad1eca37c53449.caveats: 1) Duplicate ids: 24,448 lines repeated an id already seen. In 3,233 of them the usage was not identical, against the task's assumption. Only output_tokens and thinking_tokens differed, all within the same file (streaming partials: the earlier lines carry partial counts). I kept the maximum, which equals the last line in every case. Taking the first line instead would give output 22,743,079 and thinking 9,795,774; input and cache figures do not change. 2) 144 ids appear in more than one file, all with identical usage. Each is counted once and assigned to the role of the first file the script read for it, so the role split could move by up to 144 calls. 3) 162 <synthetic> lines were skipped. 4) My first quick count of 551 files was an adding mistake; the walk finds 547 (41 main, 137 Agent-tool, 369 Workflow). 5) The cost-state check covers main files only, and only 34 of 41 have a cost-state line. Its modelUsage totals do not match the transcript counts. For example, Opus 5.5 shows 1.57B cache reads there against 2.71B in the transcripts. Two reasons are likely: subagent spend may not be folded in, and sessions written before cost-state lines existed are missing. Its modelUsage also lists haiku-5-5 with 25.2M input and claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 with 2.4M input, which never appear as transcript assistant lines (probably internal or web-search calls). So $1,302.54 is a partial sanity figure, not a complete cost. 6) Months come from UTC line timestamps. 7) The task text says 19 worktree store folders, but the glob found 18; the totals cover those 18 plus the main and OneDrive stores (20 stores).

v2:dd20ca4f8d41d2fe6cc004d50a7a389b8faa4.caveats: (1) ls -d matched 20 store folders (main, OneDrive copy, and 18 worktree folders), not 19 worktrees. (2) 75 tool_use ids appear in more than one file (likely resumed/forked session history copied into a second transcript); the script dedupes per file only, as instructed, so these 75 are counted once per file they appear in; cross-file dedupe would lower totals slightly (under 0.3 percent of calls). (3) Result size is characters of text only; image blocks count zero; ToolSearch results are ~0 chars because they return as tool_reference blocks. (4) First-word breakdown contains parsing noise from shell constructs: '(empty)' (812 calls) is commands starting with a paren, heredoc or quote, mostly inline python heredocs; for/foreach/until/timeout/import/$uv/@ are loop, function or PowerShell here-string starts, which fall to shell-other or shell-write; so shell-other (3166 calls, 7.7M chars) is inflated by these and a stricter parser would move some into shell-run/file-read/search. PowerShell cmdlets such as Get-ChildItem are NOT in the search list as specified (only Get-Content is file-read), so they land in shell-other. (5) A first-pass run with a weaker first-word parser gave slightly different shell sub-splits (e.g. file-read 6836 vs 7281 calls); the numbers reported are from the final script. (6) Tool-call counts are unaffected by classification: total 26207 calls and 91,616,905 result chars are exact for the stated dedupe rules. (7) Result characters are a proxy for context exposure, not billed tokens; a result stays in context across later turns.
